title: Potato farls with sausages and tomatoes

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Potatoes, butter, flour, oil, sausages, tomatoes and chives are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at Tesco and similar shops at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a saucepan, a frying pan and a masher, and shaping farls is well within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: 600g potatoes to 120g flour is a sound farl ratio, giving eight farls with two sausages and a tomato each for four, and the timings are realistic.

honest_times.reason: Twenty-five minutes for peeling, mashing, shaping and tending the pan, plus about 25 minutes of boiling and frying, adds up to a believable total for the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the oil and chives, is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Potato farls are the centre of the plate, and a warm cooked breakfast suits an early October morning.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are brief, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Homemade potato bread with sausages and tomatoes is a proper, filling breakfast a family would happily make again.
